comment: The glossary index — the closed kind vocabulary, the vacuous-name lexicon and the projection switches. One owner per fact: a row of a per-feature file carries a definition, an exclusion, its surfaces, its anchor and its home kind; this file carries only what every row is read against. The scopes are NOT here: they are the `feature` column of architecture/structure.tsv, read at run time (design D4). Every suffix in `vacuous` is refused in the coining kinds only, because a port role (LocationProvider) is a name the kind demands (design D7).

vacuous.reason: names who calls a thing, not what the thing does
a helper is a function that has not found its owner
a util is a package, and a package is declared in architecture/structure.tsv
info says a value carries something, never what it means
data is the shape of a value, not the word for it
an implementation is named by the port it implements
a handler names an event it does not declare
a processor names a pass over data it does not own
a provider is a port role, legal in `port` and vacuous in a coining kind
a bridge names a seam, and a seam is a `port`
a wrapper names a delegation, not a concept

projections.comment: Both on: a declared definition reaches the type that owns it as KDoc, and a `concept` row whose type no file declares is emitted as a skeleton under `skeletonRoot`/`skeletonPackage`. The generator is run by a person, never by Gradle (task 4.3).

census.comment: The three source sets of design D1 and nothing else; test sources and the native layer are out of scope, so the declaration never claims a word the project does not own. `stoplist` is the language's own vocabulary — a keyword or a platform type is not a domain word — and it is what keeps the seed's candidate set a list of terms rather than a list of tokens.
